main_text.p: responderit, sceleris admissi veniam desperaverit, eius occisionem tamen tam severe à Deo inhibitam, ut quicunque occiderit Cain, septuplum puniendus foret, quod aliqui quidem factum autumant, ut reservaretur ex Dei misericordia in poenitentiam; alii ex justitia in terroris exemplum, quorum ego neutrum inficias eo, modo illi etiam concedant, Deum hoc exemplo Ecclesiam (in ipsius vagitu quasi & incunabulis) docere voluisse, etiam in cruentos, & tyrannicos Principes, violentas manus injicere cuipiam mortalium non licere. Huic opinioni, aliquod saltem probabilitatis lumen mihi allaturum pollicetur illud Iacobi exemplum, Gen. 33. qui licet tum benedictionis paternae, tum primogeniturae Ius ex gratia divina suscepisset, & frater ipsius illi mortem post obitum patris fuisset interminatus; ita tamen naturalem primogeniturae respexit, ut non modo de vi fratri suo referenda utcunque copiis instructissimus, nihil cogitaret: {§} sed illum legatione, & per legatos munerum praesentatione praevenerit, huma-Gen. 33.

page.notes: Page is cut off at the foot: the paragraph ends with the hyphenated "huma-", which continues on the next page. The marginal note mark in the text is printed as a section sign (§), but the margin shows "g" before "Gen. 33."; the mark may be a g or a §, so I have used §, which is doubtful. "Gen. 3 3." is printed with a space between the 3s, transcribed as "33." The word "primogeniturae" was printed with a letter that looks non-Latin in the scan; I have given it in Latin letters. "licet" and "severe" are read from a small, slightly blurred print. No catchword or signature is visible. The page is a single printed page; the right-hand edge of the neighbouring page is ignored.
